answer.rationale: P99 latency spiked 5x target 2 hours after a release during peak settlement traffic. Memory_b1 shows rollback cleared a similar checkout error spike quickly with the prior stable build. Memory_b6 shows staged release gating catches bad builds early. The release timing correlates strongly with the degradation, and we have one intervention slot during peak load. Rollback is the fastest path to known-good state without dropping writes, which matches our primary objective. Circuit breakers (b4) and read replica routing (b5) address different failure modes. Capacity (b3) takes time we don't have during peak. Regional failover (b2) is costly if the issue is localized to the release. Rollback first preserves customer writes while we establish if this is release-related or load-related.
